findings_qualitative.value: ALMA resolves a compact 1.1 mm dusty disc (R~8 au), an elongated continuum jet, an asymmetric HCN 3→2 molecular ring/disc eroded along the jet direction, and one or two misaligned molecular outflows.

evidence.quote: Moreover, ALMA high spatial resolution (∼ 7 au) images of the continuum at 1.1 mm and the HCN 3→2 line resolve different gas components towards GV Tau N, a gaseous disc with R∼25 au, an ionized jet, and one (or two) molecular outflows.
In the azimuthal direction, the minimum of emission is located in the outflow direction, suggesting that the jet has eroded the circumstellar material, sweeping out the molecular gas.

findings_qualitative.value: The morphology and kinematics can be explained if GV Tau N is itself a binary whose primary has a highly inclined individual disc (i~80 deg) relative to a less inclined circumbinary gaseous disc (i~40 deg), with Jet 1 lying near the equatorial plane of the circumbinary disc.

evidence.quote: All observations can be explained if GV Tau N is binary, and the primary component has a highly inclined individual disc relative to the circumbinary disc.
The most energetic outflow, Jet 1, should be in (or close to) the equatorial plane of the circumbinary disc in order to explain the cavity cleaned of gas observed in the HCN maps.

claims.hypothesis: The circumstellar environment of GV Tau N consists of distinct physical and kinematic components that can be resolved at ~7 au scale.
claims.experiment: Image archival ALMA Cycle 4 1.1 mm continuum and HCN 3→2 line observations at ~0.06"-0.07" resolution and construct moment maps and position-velocity diagrams.
claims.result: Detected a compact 1.1 mm dust source (R~8 au, ~48 mJy), an elongated 1.1 mm continuum jet (4.6±0.5 mJy), an asymmetric HCN 3→2 ring (R_in~6 au, R_out~17-25 au) with an azimuthal minimum along Jet 1 (PA=222 deg) and Keplerian-like rotation (i~40 deg), and high-velocity outflow lobes.
claims.finding: GV Tau N hosts a compact dusty disc, an ionized jet, and a rotating gaseous circumbinary disc that is being eroded by the jet.

evidence.quote: Moreover, ALMA high spatial resolution (∼ 7 au) images of the continuum at 1.1 mm and the HCN 3→2 line resolve different gas components towards GV Tau N, a gaseous disc with R∼25 au, an ionized jet, and one (or two) molecular outflows.
In the azimuthal direction, the minimum of emission is located in the outflow direction, suggesting that the jet has eroded the circumstellar material, sweeping out the molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: GV Tau N is a misaligned binary system, which explains both the discrepancy between inner and outer disc inclinations and the presence of two misaligned outflows, one of which erodes the gaseous ring.
claims.experiment: Analyze HCN 3→2 channel maps and position-velocity diagrams along Jet 1 (PA=222 deg), Jet 2 (PA=195 deg), and perpendicular axes D1 and D2, comparing with mid-IR interferometric inclination (i=80 deg) and Keplerian curves.
claims.result: The circumbinary HCN ring matches i~40 deg (with M_*=0.8 M_sun) and is excavated along Jet 1, whereas the inner <10 au disc from VLTI/MIDI has i=80 deg and a second outflow lobe appears along Jet 2.
claims.finding: All observations can be explained if GV Tau N is a binary whose primary has a highly misaligned individual disc relative to the circumbinary disc, launching a jet nearly in the circumbinary disc plane.

evidence.quote: All observations can be explained if GV Tau N is binary, and the primary component has a highly inclined individual disc relative to the circumbinary disc.

However, we need to be cautious in our conclusions because the sensitivity and angular resolution of the HCN 3→ observations do not allow to fully disentangle Jet 2 from the gas that is accelerated in the walls of the cavity excavated by Jet 1.

claims.hypothesis: The wide velocity component of the far-IR H2O emission detected with Herschel/HIFI originates in the compact disrupted gaseous disc and outflow around GV Tau N.
claims.experiment: Decompose Herschel/HIFI water lines into wide (FWHP~8 km s^-1) and narrow (FWHP~2.7 km s^-1) Gaussians, compare the wide profile with the ALMA HCN 3→2 profile (R<0.3"), and model the p-H2O 987/1113 GHz and 1113/557 GHz line ratios under LTE.
claims.result: The p-H2O 2_02→1_11 line wings match the ALMA HCN 3→2 profile; R_obs(987/1113 GHz) = 1.0±0.1 requires optically thick emission (N(p-H2O) > 10^17 cm^-2), and an optically thick 0.5" source at T_rot~500 K predicts T_mb ~ 0.23 K in the Herschel beam, matching the observed 0.25-0.27 K.
claims.finding: The wide H2O emission is optically thick and consistent with arising from the compact disrupted gaseous disc and outflows of GV Tau N, with o-H2O emitted over a slightly larger region than p-H2O.

evidence.quote: The wings of the p-H 2 O 2 02 →1 11 line are similar to those of the interferometric HCN 3→2 line, suggesting that the origin might be similar.

assuming T rot ∼ 500 K as derived from HCN absorption observations, optically thick emission, and a source size of 0.5” (see Fig. 1), we predict T mb ∼ 0.23 K for the pH 2 O lines after diluting to the Herschel beam, which is fully consistent with Herschel observations.

claims.hypothesis: There is a strong radial chemical gradient in the HCN/13CO abundance ratio from the outer envelope to the inner few au of GV Tau N.
claims.experiment: Derive LTE column densities of 13CO and HCN from Herschel/HIFI narrow lines (~18.5" scale), PdBI/ALMA interferometric lines (R<0.18" disc scale), and compare with NIR absorption column densities (R~2-3 au scale).
claims.result: The HCN/13CO abundance ratio is ~10^-3 in the FIR envelope, ~10^-2 in the gaseous disc traced by ALMA/PdBI, and ~1 in the inner R~2-3 au probed by NIR absorption.
claims.finding: The HCN/13CO abundance ratio increases by three orders of magnitude toward the star, peaking at R~2-3 au in agreement with chemical models.

evidence.quote: As shown in Table 1, we obtain that the HCN/ [13] CO abundance ratio is ∼10 [−][3] based on the FIR observations, ∼10 [−][2] in the gaseous disc traced with ALMA and PdBI observations, and ∼1 in the close vicinity of the star where NIR molecular absorptions arise.

why_this_data.value: High spatial resolution (~7 au) ALMA interferometric images of 1.1 mm continuum and HCN 3→2 are needed to resolve the circumstellar disc and outflow kinematics that were unresolved at ~50 au in previous PdBI observations, while Herschel/HIFI provides high spectral resolution far-IR transitions of H2O, 13CO, HCN, and CN to probe water and gas excitation.

evidence.quote: Fuente et al. (2012) reported interferometric images of the HCN 3→2 and HCO [+] 3→2 lines at an angular resolution of ∼50 au. Only the HCN 3→2 emission was detected towards GV Tau N, and was interpreted as coming from the unresolved planet forming region.
Moreover, ALMA high spatial resolution (∼ 7 au) images of the continuum at 1.1 mm and the HCN 3→2 line resolve different gas components towards GV Tau N

why_this_method.value: Because Herschel/HIFI angular resolution cannot spatially resolve GV Tau N and GV Tau S or the disc from the envelope, high spectral resolution kinematic decomposition and comparison with spatially resolved ALMA HCN 3→2 line profiles are used to determine the origin of the FIR lines.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the Herschel angular resolution does not allow to resolve the two components of the binary, GV Tau N and GV Tau S, and we need to use the kinematic information to discern the origin of the observed lines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single precessing bipolar outflow vs. two different bipolar outflows to explain the misaligned red (PA=222 deg) and blue (PA=195 deg) high-velocity lobes.

evidence.quote: This misalignment can be interpreted as the consequence of a precessing bipolar outflow. Alternatively, these lobes might belong to two different bipolar outflows.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: High-velocity gas along Jet 2 being a second bipolar outflow vs. being gas associated with the walls of the cavity excavated by Jet 1.

evidence.quote: Given the angular resolution of the observations, it might also be associated to the walls of the cavity excavated by Jet 1.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Time variability of radio emission or dust thermal contamination as alternative explanations for the steep 3.6 cm to 1.1 mm spectral index (alpha ~ +1.1) of the extended jet.

evidence.quote: We should also consider the possibility that radio emission has varied on time scales of tens of years.
It would be also possible that we have overestimated the flux coming from the jet because a fraction of the extended emission is coming from dust thermal emission.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-absorption by a lower-density envelope at the systemic velocity vs. jet-disc interaction to explain the double-peaked HCN 3→2 profile.

evidence.quote: Also, self-absorption by the lower density envelope at the systemic velocity would produce the two-peak feature.

limitations_admitted.value: Non-simultaneous 3.6 cm and 1.1 mm observations and potential dust continuum contribution make the jet spectral index uncertain.

evidence.quote: Simultaneous measurements of the flux at several wavelengths would be desirable to further constrain the cm-mm spectral index.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA high spatial resolution HCN 3→2 observations filter out ~60% of the extended flux compared to PdBI.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the high spatial resolution ALMA observations recover ∼ 40% of the flux detected in PdBI observations.

limitations_admitted.value: Low signal-to-noise ratio of the PdBI 13CO 3→2 observations prevents producing a good quality spatial image.

evidence.quote: The signal-to-noise ratio of our [13] CO 3→2 observations does not allow to obtain a good quality image.

limitations_admitted.value: Herschel/HIFI angular resolution (18.5"-40") cannot spatially resolve GV Tau N from GV Tau S or measure the emitting source size directly, introducing large uncertainty in column densities.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the Herschel angular resolution does not allow to resolve the two components of the binary, GV Tau N and GV Tau S, and we need to use the kinematic information to discern the origin of the observed lines.
Again, the unknown source size introduces a large uncertainty in our calculations.

limitations_admitted.value: Sensitivity and angular resolution of the ALMA HCN 3→2 observations are insufficient to fully disentangle Jet 2 from the cavity walls of Jet 1, and stellar mass is degenerate with disc inclination.

evidence.quote: However, we need to be cautious in our conclusions because the sensitivity and angular resolution of the HCN 3→ observations do not allow to fully disentangle Jet 2 from the gas that is accelerated in the walls of the cavity excavated by Jet 1.
We recall that there is a degeneracy between the stellar mass and the inclination angle.

referee_caveats_inferred: The manual calibration and imaging parameters for ALMA project 2016.1.00813.S (weighting/robust, masks, self-calibration, continuum subtraction) are not specified beyond citing the NRAO imaging guide.

In the text (Section 4) the CN transition is referred to as CN 6->5 and 5->4 interchangeably, while Table A1 lists CN 5->4 at 566.95 GHz (note: N=5->4 is near 566.9 GHz); similarly Section 6 has a typo writing 'N(HCN)= 6.0x10^11 cm^-2' where Table 1 clarifies the second value is N(CN)= 6.0x10^11 cm^-2.
In Table A1 only one Gaussian fit per H2O line is listed despite Section 4 describing a two-component (wide + narrow) decomposition shown in Fig. 2.

Missing ~60% of the HCN 3->2 flux due to interferometric filtering in the extended ALMA configuration could affect the interpretation of the line profile shapes (such as the central dip) and the column density derived within R<0.18".

The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB (single-target Cycle 4 high-resolution ALMA Band 6 dataset 2016.1.00813.S, plus small Herschel/HIFI 1D spectra and PdBI visibilities)
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project code (2016.1.00813.S) and Herschel observation ID (OT1_afuente_2) are publicly available, and the analysis steps (2D Gaussian fit, moment maps, PV diagrams, Gaussian line fits, and LTE column density estimates) are straightforward. However, the ALMA data were manually calibrated and imaged without stating the weighting, robust parameter, self-calibration, or continuum subtraction details, and the PdBI dataset is not directly linked.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Cycle 4 dataset (2016.1.00813.S) is public in the ALMA archive, and the core ALMA results—compact 1.1 mm continuum flux (~48 mJy) and size (94x66 mas), extended jet flux (4.6 mJy), HCN 3->2 ring radii (0.04"-0.18"), integrated flux (~1.4 Jy/beam km/s), and PV diagram kinematics—are concrete quantitative measurements that an agent can attempt to reproduce from the raw archival data.
